findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` checks `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` (line 70). Because `hasPermission` returns `true` if any of the passed scopes are granted on the `Groups` resource, an administrator who has only been granted the `view` scope on all groups will have `canManage()` evaluate to `true`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards top-level group creation and group moves with `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so any user with `view` permission on all groups can create and move top-level groups. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at lines 75-76 should be updated accordingly).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in GroupPermissionsV2 never finds group resources and returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body:
In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (lines 121-125), `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` is used to iterate over group resources, and inside the consumer `groupResource.getId()` is passed to `hasPermission(...)` and added to `granted`. There are three bugs here:
1. When per-group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 121-127), `resource.setType(...)` is never called, so individual group resources have `type == null` (only the all-groups resource created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` has `type = "Groups"`). `findByType` therefore never matches any individual group resource.
2. `groupResource.getName()` holds the `GroupModel` ID (set in `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`), whereas `groupResource.getId()` is the internal authorization `Resource` UUID. Passing `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, which will not find the resource by name, and adding `groupResource.getId()` to `granted` returns `Resource` UUIDs instead of group IDs to `UserModel.GROUPS` search filters.
3. For the `Groups` resource type resource itself (`name == "Groups"`), `granted.add(...)` would add the resource UUID rather than actual group IDs.

findings.title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName does not resolve Group (or Client) resource names
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 328-350) only handles `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` and otherwise falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()`. When a group resource is created in `getOrCreateResource`, its `name` is set to the group's UUID (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()`) and `displayName` is not set. As a result, fetching policy/permission representations for `Groups` resources will return `null` (or the raw UUID) as the resource name instead of `"All groups"` or the group's name/path.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
findings.body: On line 133 of `GroupPermissionEvaluator.java`, the Javadoc for `void requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.
